name: Mewing Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Mangroves of mangaia island (southern cook islands)
description: A chunky, large-billed kingfisher with a greenish crown, cheek, and back and bluish wings and tail. White underneath with a strongly orange wash to the eyebrow and neck.

name: Mexican Duck
rangeDescription: Southeastern arizona, southern new mexico and western texas (trans-pecos region) southward to central mexico
description: Both sexes look like a dark-colored female Mallard. Bill of male is dull yellowish; bill of female is mottled orange and black, like a typical Mallard.

name: Thick-billed Spiderhunter
rangeDescription: Forest of peninsular thailand, malay peninsula, sumatra, and borneo
description: Dull and largely unmarked spiderhunter. Brownish olive above with a yellow belly, faint yellow crescents around the eye, and faint speckling on the crown.

name: Blue-capped Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: Northern moluccas (halmahera, ternate, bacan, and adjacent islands)
description: A small, mostly green fruit-dove with a blue forecrown and a yellow undertail. Blue forehead is bolder in males, bordered with a thin, well-defined yellow line.

name: Gray-backed Tachuri
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (central bahia to minas gerais and northern são paulo)
description: A small rare and endemic flycatcher with a conspicuous white patch in front of the eyes and a short white eyebrow. Also note its gray crown and a brownish-gray back and cinnamon washed breast and sides.

name: Green-crowned Plovercrest
rangeDescription: Eastern brazil (southern minas gerais to espírito santo and northeastern são paulo)
description: Medium-sized hummingbird with an iridescent green body and short bill. Males have a long iridescent green crest, a violet throat that extends down the belly, flanked in gray.

name: Diamond Firetail
rangeDescription: Southeastern australia (east-central queensland to southern victoria and southeastern south australia)
description: Plump, tiny bird with olive back, gray head, white belly and throat, white-spotted black flanks, black breast band, and bright red bill in adult. In flight, bright red rump apparent.

name: Lesser Seedcracker
rangeDescription: Eastern tanzania to southern malawi, eastern zimbabwe, and northern mozambique
description: A colorful, chunky waxbill with a large conical bill. Both sexes have a red hood and tail, but females have slightly less extensive red.

name: Black-throated Prinia
rangeDescription: Eastern nepal to sikkim, bhutan, southeastern tibet, and arunachal pradesh
description: Very long tailed prinia of hilly and montane areas, descending to foothills in winter. Plain with brown upperparts, slightly rustier on the wing, and paler belly.

name: Socotra Warbler
rangeDescription: Socotra (off eastern somalia)
description: Drab little warbler endemic to Socotra. Gray-brown above and pale gray below, sometimes showing a brighter rufous coloration crown.

name: Little Inca-Finch
rangeDescription: Foothills of arid western peru (middle río marañón drainage)
description: The smallest of the five species of inca-finch, found only in the hot lower elevations of the Marañon Valley in the Andes of northern Peru. Handsome adult has a yellow bill and legs, a black mask, a rusty back, and white outer tail feathers that may only be evident in flight.

name: Little Buttonquail
rangeDescription: Grassland and woodland throughout australia
description: Small, pale buttonquail with pale eye and thick bill, found in grassland habitats across inland Australia. In some years, this species is very common; in others, it can be very scarce.

name: Corsican Nuthatch
rangeDescription: Montane pine forest of corsica
description: Endemic to the island of Corsica, where it is the sole nuthatch species. Small, gray above and pale below with a long bill.

name: Cape Bulbul
rangeDescription: South africa (southern and southwestern cape province)
description: A typical open-country African bulbul that is uniform ashy-brown in coloration with a yellow undertail and a conspicuous and diagnostic whitish eye-ring. Pairs and small groups forage in coastal scrub, fynbos, and gardens, eating a variety of fruit and invertebrates.

name: Red Lark
rangeDescription: South africa (northwestern northern cape)
description: A medium-large, chunky lark that has a rounded head lacking a crest, a short strong bill, a bold face pattern, and a heavily blotched chest. Color often matches the prevailing soil color in the region, varying from brick-red in areas of red sand dunes to rusty-brown in areas of shale and clay plains.

name: Sooty Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Southeastern bolivia to central argentina, eastern paraguay, uruguay, and southern brazil
description: A very small and long-tailed flycatcher with fairly uniformly dark-gray plumage. It has a dark bill and legs with a slightly paler throat and two indistinct wingbars.

name: Seram Oriole
rangeDescription: Seram (southern moluccas)
description: A dull, entirely olive-brown oriole with a pale collar and a conspicuous dark face. Singles or pairs can be found in forest and forest edge in the lowlands and foothills, being more abundant lower down.

name: Crestless Curassow
rangeDescription: Guyana to southern venezuela, eastern colombia, and adjacent northwestern brazil
description: Large, terrestrial bird of flood-prone lowland rainforest; generally shy and difficult to see. Note all-dark appearance and small, red bill.

name: Buru Thrush
rangeDescription: Mid-mountain forest of buru (southern moluccas)
description: A distinctive thrush with chocolate-brown upperparts, a dark head with a conspicuous pale eye-ring, a black throat, and a white belly. Also shows rows of clean white spots on wings.

name: Sooty Thrush
rangeDescription: Mountains of costa rica and western panama (far western chiriquí)
description: Very dark montane thrush. Robin-sized, all black with white eye and yellow eyering, bill, and legs.
